title: Isolation of nuclei from frozen human subcutaneous adipose tissue for full-length single-nuclei transcriptional profiling
protocol: Add 2 mL of homogenization buffer into glass vessel and place on ice in a beaker.
Pulverize 100 mg of frozen human subcutaneous WAT in liquid nitrogen using a mortar and pestle.
Cool the mortar and pestle with LN2 by pouring LN2 into the mortar until full, let it evaporate, and repeat once for a total of two times.
Place spatula in a separate mortar and pour LN2 over it.
Top up LN2 during pulverization process to keep spatula cool.
Re-fill mortar with LN2 and place 100mg of WAT in the mortar.
Keep sample on dry ice until placed in the mortar.
Pulverize tissue by firmly pressing down on WAT with pestle for approximately 50 strokes.
Top up LN2 (approximately twice) to ensure equipment and tissue stay cold during pulverization.
Tilt the mortar towards the lip and let LN2 evaporate.
Use a LN2 cooled spatula to scrape the pulverized WAT into a glass vessel containing 2 mL of homogenization buffer.
Homogenize the mixture with an automated dounce homogenizer by performing 12 strokes forward and 12 strokes backward.
Transfer the homogenate equally to two 1.7 mL LoBind tubes.
Clean the glass vessel with 400 μL of homogenization buffer and add it to the LoBind tubes containing the homogenate.
Add 12 μL of 10% Triton X-100 to each 1.7 mL LoBind tube to achieve a final concentration of 0.1% Triton X-100 (v/v).
Pulse vortex the mixture in each LoBind tube.
Leave on ice for 30 minutes, protecting from light and pulse vortex every 5 minutes.
Place a 100μm filter over a 50mL conical tube.
Place a 40μm filter over another 50mL conical tube.
Pre-wet each filter with 100μL PBS (−/−).
Filter homogenate solution through the 100μm filter into the 50mL conical tube.
Use 400μL homogenization buffer to wash any remaining homogenate from the LoBind tubes and transfer it through the 100μm filter.
Pipette homogenate solution through the 40μm filter into the 50mL conical tube.
Dispense filtered homogenate solution equally into pre-chilled 2 x 1.7mL LoBind Tubes.
Centrifuge the homogenates at 2700g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Remove lipid layer by carefully pipetting off using a P1000 tip.
Resuspend 50 μl of homogenate solution in each 1.7 ml LoBind tube thoroughly with pipetting up and down (approximately 30 times).
Transfer homogenate solution to pre-chilled 1.7 ml LoBind tube.
Repeat resuspension for second tube containing homogenate solution, pipetting up and down approximately 30 times.
Transfer homogenate solution to pre-chilled 1.7mL LoBind tube used in step 13b.
Add 100 μL homogenization buffer to the homogenate solution and mix by pipetting.
Centrifuge the homogenate at 2700g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and leave approximately 50 μL.
Resuspend 50 μL pellet thoroughly by pipetting up and down (approximately 30 times).
Add 950 μL of Nuclei Resuspension buffer and mix with pipetting.
Centrifuge the nuclei at 2700g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and leave approximately 50 μL.
Resuspend 50 μL pellet thoroughly by pipetting up and down (approximately 30 times).
Add 450 μL of Nuclei Resuspension buffer and mix with pipetting.
Filter nuclei solution through a 25g syringe 10 times.
Be careful not to let the 25g syringe touch the plastic of the 1.7mL LoBind tube.
Add 1 drop of ReadyProbes NucBlue (Hoechst 33342) to the 500 μL nuclei solution.
Leave on ice protected from light for 15 min.
Mix nuclei solution with pipetting before immediately adding 10 μL of nuclei solution to Countess slide.
Count nuclei with Countess 3 Automated Cell Counter.
Dilute the sample with DPBS (−/−) to achieve a final concentration of 200K nuclei/mL for validation on ICELL8 CX platform.
Mix nuclei preparation with reagents from TakaraBio USA SMART-Seq® ICELL8® Application Kit – 5 Chip and DPBS (−/−) to achieve a final concentration of 40K nuclei/mL.
Dispense nuclei solution onto ICELL8 350v chip as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Use ICELL8 CellSelect software to confirm single nucleus candidacy.
Check nanowells for the presence of a single nucleus according to settings in Table 1.
Select nanowells containing a single nucleus for downstream processing.
Exclude nanowells void of nuclei or with more than one nucleus.
Identify false negatives and manually push through using cellselect software if necessary.
Prepare single nuclei RNA-Seq libraries following manufacturer's recommendation.
Sequence two snRNA-Seq libraries simultaneously using Illumina HiSeq 4000.
Aim for 250 million paired-end reads per library.
Ensure compatibility with any Illumina sequencing platform using dual 8nt barcode.
Typically, sequence two snRNA-libraries (index A kit and index B kit) on a single HiSeq lane.
